description.narrative: The most significant Project level outcomes are stakeholders - improved livelihood for smallholder farmers. IFC's investment in the project is expected to support the livelihoods of a significant number of smallholder farmers in Cote d'Ivoire who supply cocoa beans to SUCDEN. Cocoa farming is a critical sector for the country's economy, but many cocoa farmers in Cote d'Ivoire are among the poorest in the country. SUCDEN's pre-harvest finance provides farmer suppliers with access to funds for fertilizers, pruning, and farm upkeep, and IFC is discussing an Advisory Services program to support SUCDEN's efforts towards compliance with the European Union Deforestation Regulation. Beyond the Project, IFC expects SUCDEN's sustainability programs to cocoa farmers to positively impact cocoa quality, the efficiency and effectiveness of cocoa production, and the supply of sustainable and traceable cocoa. These outcomes can contribute to promoting the competitiveness and sustainability of the cocoa sector in Cote d'Ivoire.

The proposed investment is an up to 250 million syndicated term loan (1-year maturity, renewable/re-committed annually, for up to 4 years in aggregate) by IFC to SUCDEN Cote dIvoire (SUCDEN-CI or the Company) and its parent company SUCDEN S.A (the co-Borrower and, jointly with SUCDEN-CI and other subsidiaries, SUCDEN or the Group) to finance the procurement and export of cocoa beans from Cote dIvoire (CI).
